# EMET — Gospel of Mary, Chapter 9
**Agent:** EMET (Literal/Transparent)
**Source:** P.Berol. 8502, Gospel of Mary, p. 14 (partial) | Coptic
**Chapter:** 9

---

[Pages 11-14 are mostly lost. Only the very end of page 14 survives, giving us the tail of chapter 9 mid-sentence. The chapter opening and most of its content are absent.]

**9:1** [...]"...and desire that, 'I did not see you descending, but now I see you ascending. Why do you lie, since you belong to me?'

**9:2** "The soul answered and said, 'I saw you. You did not see me nor recognize me. I served you as a garment, and you did not know me.'

**9:3** "When it had said this, it went away rejoicing greatly."

---

*Translator's Note (EMET):* The surviving fragment captures the soul's confrontation with the power of Desire. EMET retains "garment" (*stolē*) — the soul served as a vestment/cloak for Desire without Desire knowing the soul within. The soul's final departure "rejoicing greatly" anticipates its liberation.
